headlines.title: AI just saved SpaceX: record $14.6B quarter, possible merger
headlines.summary: SpaceX just reported $14.6 billion in quarterly revenue and the first profit in its history, and the surprise is where the money came from: AI. Host Ejaaz Ahamadeen breaks down how SpaceX became the number one neocloud renting compute to Anthropic and Google, the power bottleneck, the potential Tesla merger, and what could still go wrong.

headlines.title: Qualcomm (QCOM) Stock Stays Near Fair Value On Tokenized Trading Objections
headlines.summary: QUALCOMM has delivered a powerful long run for shareholders, and with the stock last closing at US$177.96, the real question for you now is whether that price still lines up with the cash flows the business can produce over time. QUALCOMM has returned 81.0% over the past 3 years, which puts a lot of accumulated optimism on the line if its future cash generation does not keep pace with that share price performance.

headlines.title: AMD, QCOM Targets Raised While INTC, COHR Face Cuts — Susquehanna Sees ‘Modest Upside’ For Chip Earnings
headlines.summary: Susquehanna expects AI demand to drive semiconductor earnings upside in the third quarter, even as its price-target revisions diverge across major chipmakers.

headlines.title: Qualcomm (QCOM): Automotive Growth Meets Pressure on Handset Earnings
headlines.summary: QUALCOMM Incorporated (NASDAQ:QCOM) sells more technology into vehicles while its larger smartphone business weakens. That makes automotive diversification important, but it raises a practical question: can the new growth get big enough to protect overall profits?

headlines.title: Qualcomm Announces Quarterly Cash Dividend
headlines.summary: Qualcomm Incorporated (NASDAQ: QCOM) today announced a quarterly cash dividend of $0.92 per common share, payable on December 17, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 3, 2026.

description: QUALCOMM Incorporated engages in the development and commercialization of foundational technologies for the wireless industry worldwide. It operates through three segments: Qualcomm CDMA Technologies (QCT); Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL); and Qualcomm Strategic Initiatives (QSI). The QCT segment develops and supplies integrated circuits and system software with connectivity and computing technologies for use in mobile devices; automotive systems for connectivity, digital cockpit, and ADAS/AD; and IoT, including consumer electronic devices, industrial devices, and edge networking products. The QTL segment grants licenses or provides rights to use portions of its intellectual property portfolio, which include various patent rights useful in the manufacture and sale of wireless products comprising products implementing LTE, and/or OFDMA-based 5G products and derivatives; to use cellular standard-essential patents, including 3G, 4G and 5G for cellular devices. The QSI segment invests in early-stage companies in various industries, including 5G, artificial intelligence, automotive, consumer, enterprise, cloud, IoT, and extended reality, and investments, including non-marketable equity securities and, to a lesser extent, marketable equity securities, and convertible debt instruments. It also provides development, and other services and sells related products to the United States government agencies and their contractors. In addition, the company is also involved in Qualcomm government technologies and data center businesses. Further, it provides security and intelligence services for unmanaged networks through software-based network security solutions. The company is in collaboration with Amazon to enable customized silicon at scale for large-scale AI data centers. QUALCOMM Incorporated was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in San Diego, California.
